deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct. It is a German prose text in Kurrent script: the opening of a schoolbook-style outline of ancient world history ('Die alte Weltgeschichte').

Content, in order:
(1) A definition: ancient world history is a complete, systematic narration of the most important events on Earth since its creation.
(2) The Earth has changed since creation in two ways.
  (a) Through humans: they built huts, houses, villages and towns, levelled mountains, cut down forests, drained marshes, changed the courses of rivers, and built dwellings on the water (ships).
  (b) Through nature: earthquakes destroyed whole countries, floods tore land away, other natural phenomena raised land from the sea, and some regions became fertile while others became barren.
(3) Cultivated countries have become wild again, and once-ignorant peoples are now the most enlightened and educated.
(4) Heading 'Gang der Kultur' (course of civilisation). Asia, where the first humans were created, was the first place peoples developed. There they founded towns through arts and sciences and traded. Asia is called among the most important parts of the world. The Assyrians, Israelites and Persians stood out as warriors; the sentence breaks off, and the next page continues that the Chaldeans stood out in another field.

The next page continues the standard Enlightenment 'translatio' scheme of civilisation moving from Asia to Africa to Europe.

The hand, style and content are those of a school exercise or lecture notes. The page is probably not by Gauss himself; it may be a notebook kept in the Gauss family, possibly by one of his children around 1816, but that is unsure. The bundle name 'HB.Lagrange1816' is evidently a shelf or bundle label, not a description of the content.
errors: No mathematical derivations, so no mathematical errors to assess.
Content-wise this is conventional late-18th/early-19th-century school historiography (creationist chronology; Asia→Africa→Europe course of culture); not 'errors' in the mathematical sense.

results.what: Non-mathematical school-style notes on ancient world history and the 'course of culture' (Asia → Africa → Europe)
results.modern_name: Enlightenment universal-history / translatio studii schema (school textbook genre)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics at all. It is a routine school-history exercise, likely not even in Gauss's own hand, so nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematical work.
transcription_corrections: Line 8–9: 'Bäume[?] zu Moräste[?] ausgetrocknet' more likely reads 'Seen und Moräste ausgetrocknet' (drained lakes and marshes).
Line 12: the inserted mark after 'ganze' is an insertion caret, not '&c.'. The sense is 'durch Erdbeben ganze Länder zu Grunde gerichtet'.
Lines 14–15: 'aus dem durch eben[?] Meere hervorgeholt' is likely 'Länder aus dem Meere hervorgeholt'. The 'durch eben' is probably a misreading of the above-line insertion.
Line 17: the sentence 'welche sehr kultiviert waren, sind ganz verwildert' needs a subject such as 'Länder' (possibly omitted by the writer). 'ganz verwildert' may read 'nun verwildert'.
Line 19: 'am klärsten' is probably 'am aufgeklärtesten' or 'am klügsten'; it is uncertain.
Lines 24–26 are garbled. The sense is roughly that Asia was the most important ('wichtigste') among all parts of the world ('unter allen Welttheilen').
Last line: 'sich zeichneten sich als' should read 'hingegen zeichneten sich als' (continued on the next page with the Chaldeans).
